input: # divergent.tsv -- where this repo's THREE ports DISAGREE, executed.
#   input  CSS source. Escapes \n \r \t \\ are decoded, as in spec/.
#   ts,go,rust
#          what each port produces TODAY: the AST as JSON, or ERROR:<code>.
#   opts   plugin options as JSON, empty for the defaults.
#   why    what causes it, and which port the repair belongs to.
# NOT A FIXTURE, and deliberately NOT under spec/: all three runtimes run
# every file in spec/ by directory listing, and every row here is a row one
# of them is expected to fail. A fixture fails when behaviour REGRESSES;
# this fails BOTH ways, because a port repaired to agree with the others
# still faces a register claiming they differ, so the suite goes red and
# names the row to delete. A divergence recorded as a passing test of
# current behaviour survives its own repair with nothing red, which is how
# the 2026-08 fleet audit found 29 recorded claims contradicted by
# execution. ADR-14 is the rule; this file is the half that runs.
# Every column is EXECUTED: ts/test/divergent.test.ts reads `ts`,
# go/divergent_test.go reads `go`, rs/tests/divergent.rs reads `rust`.
# Until this file existed, the three rows below lived in AGENTS.md prose,
# with only the Rust side asserted (rs/tests/css.rs) -- so the Go values,
# which are what makes each row a divergence, were measurements nothing
# re-took.
# TypeScript is canonical (AGENTS.md, "Authority and alignment rules"), so
# the repair for every row here is in the Go port, and the Rust column
# tracks `ts` by construction rather than by coincidence.
@media x {a{b:c}}
why: ECMAScript trim keeps U+0085 (NEL) in a prelude; Go's strings.TrimSpace, which is Unicode White_Space, drops it. Repair: Go trims the ECMAScript set.

input: ﻿a{b:c}
why: The reverse code point: U+FEFF is ECMAScript whitespace and is not Unicode White_Space, so TS trims the BOM out of the selector and Go keeps it. Repair: Go.

input: p { color:; }
why: A declaration with an empty value never runs the action that records an end. TS leaves it undefined, which JSON drops; Go emits null. Repair: Go omits the key.

input: @host\\
why: A trailing backslash is an escape whose character is missing, so the scanners step one past the end. TS counts that step in the column while taking a clamped substring; Go's clampLen clamps before the column arithmetic. Repair: decide the intended TS column, then make both match it.
